blocks.text: In Cairo you will spend a lot of time asking for the road, taking taxi, metro and microbus, and understanding directions given quickly:ḫušš yimīn, w-ba'dēn ʿala ṭūl…». In this unit learn the Egyptian imperative (iktib, rūḥ, ḫud, taʿāla) and its negation (ma-truḥš), the words of the directions and the phrases to move by means. Six weeks, in parallel with ONO-03, B1-15 and B1-16.

rows: 8–9 hours · six weeks (weeks 125–130), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or Egyptian conversation partner, a map of Cairo (also online)
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. to form the affirmative and negative imperative, to a man, to a woman, to several persons;
2. use the most frequent irregular imperatives (taʿāla, hāt, ḫud, kul);
3. ask for the road and understand directions (right, left, straight, traffic light, square);
4. take a taxi, the metro and the microbus: give the address, ask for the price, let you leave;
5. ask and give practical advice on travel.
Six-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).

chapters.title: 2. The Egyptian imperative and the fuṣḥā

blocks.text: ⁧لَا تَذْهَبْ⁩ ma-truḥš Don't go.
As in fuṣḥā, the imperative has three forms: male, female (-i), plural (-u). The dual doesn't exist.
The imperative is formed by the imperfect (EGY-03) by removing the prefix: tiktib → iktib . In front of two consonants one i is added.
timši imši imši imšu

Concave verbs (rūḥ, šūf, ʾūl, nām) do not need the initials: the long vowel is enough. The verbs of four letters (itkallim, istanna, ḫalli "Leave', "Nazzil', "Leave': the imperative is identical to the base: ḫalli l-bāʾi Keep the rest of it, you nazzilni hina, let me get down here.
look buṣṣ buṣṣi buṣṣu
Denial is done with ma- + imperfect without b- + -š (such as the present negative, EGY-03):

To soften the imperative. The nude imperative can sound rude with strangers. Law is added samaḥt (f. law samaḥti), min faḍlak , or mumkin + imperfect is used: mumkin tiddīni T-tazkara? Can you give me the ticket?

blocks.text: The microbus (mikrobāṣ) is the collective minibus that follows fixed routes but without marked stops: we ask the driver or the passengers where it goes (rāyiḥ...?) and asks to come down when needed. usṭa is the way to turn to a driver or artisan. Apps. In Cairo many use transport apps with a fixed price; is the easiest way for a foreigner to avoid bargaining. Available apps change: check active apps before leaving.

The beginning of the imperative. iktib, inzil, imši: the i is short and weak; after a word that ends in vowel falls: ya Lūka, ktib! ḫušš and buṣṣ. The double finale is heard: ḫušš, buṣṣ, ḫuš, buṣ. Shadowing. The tutor reads the directions of Yāsmīn the natural rhythm; You repeat them, then you tell them by following the path with your finger on a map.
